## pluggable_component

```yaml
name: select_batch
return_type: List[int]
signature_template: select_batch(model, x_unlabeled, x_labeled, batch_size, seed,
  *paradigm_extras_by_name) -> List[int]
contract:
  fixed_positional_args:
  - model
  - x_unlabeled
  - x_labeled
  - batch_size
  seed_param: seed
  paradigm_extras_forwarding: by_name_from_config
  forbidden_param_names:
  - config
  - batch_output
  - batch_outputs
rationale: "Bayesian-AL methods are multi-step per acquisition round: they score\n\
  uncertainty (via MC dropout / posterior samples) but also reason about\ndiversity\
  \ or representativeness with respect to the already-labeled set\n(e.g., GBALD's\
  \ Eq. 13 computes distances to labeled-set penultimate\nfeatures). The pluggable\
  \ function therefore needs read access to\n`x_labeled` so it can implement what\
  \ the paper describes. Methods that\nonly need uncertainty (e.g., vanilla BALD)\
  \ accept the parameter and\nignore it; the cost of a one-extra-positional-arg is\
  \ small compared to\nthe cost of silently degrading multi-step methods to pure top-k.\n\
  \nStateless beyond the signature: the function must NOT mutate `x_labeled`\nor store\
  \ it \u2014 it's read-only state passed in by the notebook each round.\n"
```

## arch_contract_requirements

```yaml
description: Spec-derived active-learning architecture contract requirements. Concrete
  shapes remain paper/code-derived; this only validates the universal AL contract
  surface.
required_blocks:
  data_loader.load_data_returns:
    type: dict[str, shape_string]
    min_keys:
    - x_pool
    - y_pool
    - x_test
    - y_test
    exact_keys:
    - x_pool
    - y_pool
    - x_test
    - y_test
  architecture.model:
    required_subblocks:
    - class_name
    - forward.input
    - forward.output_type
  pluggable_component.name:
    must_equal: spec.comparison.pluggable_component.name
  pluggable_component.input_shapes:
    type: dict[str, shape_string]
    min_keys:
    - x_unlabeled
  pluggable_component.output_shape:
    type: shape_string
  training_loop.function_name:
    must_equal: train_from_scratch
  training_loop.input_shapes:
    type: dict[str, shape_string]
    min_keys:
    - x_train
    - y_train
symbol_conventions:
  B: runtime batch size inside model forward
  N: training-set size
  N_test: test-set size
  N_pool: unlabeled pool size
  n_features: input feature dim
  n_classes: number of classes
  hidden_dim: model hidden width when applicable
```

## notebook_layout

```yaml
description: 'Section structure for active-learning notebooks. Each section is a

  declarative description of what the notebook-generator emits at that

  position; the actual cells are written by the agent based on

  method_spec.json + paper_map.json + the generated method/ package.

  '
sections:
- id: title
  title: Paper title (from spec.paper.title)
  kind: agnostic
  content: 'Markdown-only. Top-level # heading with the paper''s full citation

    (authors, year, venue), a short ''what this notebook gives you'' bullet

    list, a ''two ways to use this'' bullet list (run-as-is vs. import from

    own code), and a ''what this notebook does NOT do'' note (this is a

    reference implementation, not a benchmark reproduction; defer to the

    paper for empirical claims).

    '
- id: install
  title: '## 0. Install dependencies (first run only)'
  kind: agnostic
  content: "One markdown cell explaining when to run, one code cell running\n`%pip\
    \ install -r requirements.txt` (NOT `!pip` \u2014 the magic is needed\non systems\
    \ where `pip` is not in the shell PATH). Cell can sit live;\nrunning on an already-installed\
    \ system is a no-op.\n"
- id: setup
  title: '## 1. Setup'
  kind: agnostic
  content: "One code cell: `%matplotlib inline`, imports (matplotlib.pyplot, numpy,\n\
    torch, then `from method import (...)` listing the public API the\nnotebook calls),\
    \ master `SEED = 42`, seed numpy + torch globals.\nThe import list is determined\
    \ from method/__init__.py's __all__;\nany helper used in \xA74 must be exported\
    \ there.\n"
- id: parameters
  title: '## 2. Parameters'
  kind: agnostic
  content: "Markdown header explaining the provenance schema (paper / system_default\n\
    / system_inferred), then the **rendered provenance table FIRST**, then\nthe params\
    \ dict code cell, then an \"Optional: scale up to paper-faithful\nvalues\" subsection\
    \ with a commented-out cfg.update() block.\nTable-first ordering: readers scan\
    \ provenance at a glance; code is\nbelow for editing. Table is generated once\
    \ at notebook-build time from\nthe params dict and embedded as static markdown\
    \ \u2014 does not auto-update\nif the user edits params downstream.\n"
- id: setup_pieces
  title: '## 3. The setup pieces'
  kind: paradigm
  content: "Brief overview markdown that names the substrate (model + training +\n\
    data + bootstrap) and explicitly tells the reader: \"these are paper\nprotocol\
    \ but NOT the paper's contribution; skim and move on to \xA74\".\nMention any\
    \ paradigm-specific architecture requirements (for AL/bayesian:\ndropout active\
    \ at inference; for AL/batch_acquisition: forward_with_embedding\ncontract). Pull\
    \ these from the matched paradigm's `pluggable_component`\nand `architecture`\
    \ blocks.\n"
  subsections:
  - id: data
    title: '### 3.1 Data'
    content: "One paragraph explaining `load_data()` defaults to\nmethod/example_data/,\
      \ downloads MNIST on first run, points to \xA76\nfor custom data. One code cell\
      \ calling load_data with cfg-derived\nargs, printing pool/test/classes shapes.\n"
  - id: model
    title: '### 3.2 Model'
    content: 'One paragraph naming the paper''s architecture choice and what

      we ship vs. swap-in options. Highlight the paradigm-specific

      constraint (e.g., ''forward_with_embedding hook'' for batch_acquisition,

      ''dropout active at inference'' for bayesian). One code cell:

      `model = build_model(...); print(model)` to show the architecture.

      '
  - id: training
    title: '### 3.3 Training'
    content: "One paragraph naming the protocol (Adam, retrain-from-scratch,\ntrain-until-99%,\
      \ paper section reference). NO code cell \u2014 training\nhappens per-round\
      \ in \xA73.4 (bootstrap) and \xA75.1 (the loop). State\nthis explicitly so the\
      \ reader doesn't expect a cell.\n"
  - id: bootstrap
    title: '### 3.4 Bootstrap labeled set'
    content: "For AL: pick `initial_labeled` random examples (or run a method-\nspecific\
      \ bootstrap routine if the spec declares one \u2014 e.g.,\nGBALD's `construct_core_set`),\
      \ train a warmup model on them.\nThe warmup model is what \xA74's per-component\
      \ demos use. If the\nmethod has a Stage-1-style initialization (like GBALD),\
      \ call it\nhere and reference \xA74.x for the algorithmic explanation.\n"
- id: method
  title: "## 4. The {method_name} method \u2B50"
  kind: method_specific
  content: "The paper's contribution, broken into the method's own components.\nFirst\
    \ subsection is always 'Intuition' \u2014 a markdown cell motivating\nWHY the\
    \ method's design choice solves the problem. Subsequent\nsubsections come from\
    \ the spec's method components (paper-element IDs\nin paper_map.json grouped by\
    \ algorithmic function). Each component-\nsubsection has: (a) markdown explaining\
    \ the math with paper section/\nequation references in **bold**, (b) a code cell\
    \ exercising that piece\non the warmup model from \xA73.4 (small visualization\
    \ or printed output\nshowing the piece does what it says). Final subsection is\
    \ 'Putting it\ntogether' \u2014 markdown + small code block showing how the wrapper\n\
    composes the components. Mark novel pieces with \u2B50 (the paper's actual\ncontribution;\
    \ method components that are off-the-shelf \u2014 e.g., k-MEANS++\nin BADGE \u2014\
    \ get cited but no \u2B50).\n"
  generator_instructions: "Walk paper_map.json's element list. Group elements by their\
    \ algorithmic\nfunction: motivation/intuition (concept-* IDs), distinct novel\
    \ pieces\n(each with its own subsection \u2014 typically eq-* or alg-* IDs), and\
    \ the\nwrapper. For each piece, the markdown cell cites the paper element's\n\
    `section` field. The exercise code cell uses helpers from\n`method.method` (compute_gradient_embeddings,\
    \ kmeans_plus_plus_seeding,\netc.) \u2014 these must be in method/__init__.py\
    \ or accessible via\nmethod.method to be imported in \xA71.\n"
- id: running
  title: '## 5. Running active learning end-to-end'
  kind: paradigm
  content: "One paragraph naming the experimental protocol from the paper's\nSection\
    \ 4 (Experiments). State that `labeled` and `unlabeled` continue\nfrom \xA73.4's\
    \ bootstrap state.\n"
  subsections:
  - id: loop
    title: '### 5.1 The acquisition loop'
    content: "Define `evaluate(model, x, y)` (eval mode, no_grad, argmax accuracy),\n\
      then run the AL loop. Two things here are correctness-critical and\nhave silently\
      \ broken past runs (they don't crash and the learning\ncurve still rises, so\
      \ they pass smoke) \u2014 follow them exactly:\n\n(1) RETRAIN FROM SCRATCH each\
      \ round. Build a FRESH model with\n    `build_model(...)` at the TOP of every\
      \ round, then\n    `train_from_scratch` it on the current labeled set. Do NOT\
      \ carry\n    one model object across rounds (and do NOT reuse \xA73.4's warmup\n\
      \    model) \u2014 that is warm-starting, which BADGE and most modern AL\n \
      \   explicitly avoid because it changes the algorithmic regime. (Only\n    if\
      \ the paper deliberately warm-starts should you reuse the model \u2014\n   \
      \ follow `spec.critical_requirements.training` and say so.)\n\n(2) INDEX BOOKKEEPING.\
      \ `select_batch` returns positions INTO the\n    tensor you passed it (the current\
      \ unlabeled pool) \u2014 NOT global\n    pool indices. Keep an explicit array\
      \ of the unlabeled examples'\n    global indices and map back through it. NEVER\
      \ recover globals with\n    positional-offset arithmetic (e.g. `i - len(initial_indices)`),\n\
      \    which falsely assumes the labeled set is a contiguous prefix of\n    the\
      \ pool. Keep `labeled`/`unlabeled` as DISJOINT index sets (set\n    difference\
      \ on update) so an already-labeled example can never be\n    re-selected.\n\n\
      (3) ACQUISITION-ROUND SEMANTICS. `cfg[\"num_rounds\"]` means the\n    number\
      \ of acquisition rounds, not the number of plotted\n    evaluation points. Evaluate\
      \ the initial labeled set once before\n    any acquisition, then acquire exactly\
      \ once per round and append\n    the post-acquisition evaluation. The resulting\
      \ learning curve\n    has `cfg[\"num_rounds\"] + 1` points. Do NOT guard the\
      \ final\n    `select_batch` call with `r < cfg[\"num_rounds\"] - 1`, and do\n\
      \    NOT acquire a final batch that is never evaluated.\n    Do NOT evaluate\
      \ before the label merge and then append that\n    accuracy with the post-merge\
      \ `len(labeled_idx)`; the label\n    count and accuracy must describe the same\
      \ trained model state.\n\n(4) VISIBLE ACQUISITION STATE. The notebook owns the\
      \ active-learning\n    state. If a method needs an initialization/core-set/bootstrap\n\
      \    acquisition step, call the helper once in \xA73.4 and record those\n  \
      \  returned indices in `labeled_idx`. The per-round\n    `select_batch(...)`\
      \ call must return every new unlabeled\n    position that should become labeled\
      \ that round. Do NOT rely on\n    `select_batch` to internally add extra unlabeled\
      \ examples to a\n    temporary labeled set and then return only a later subset;\
      \ that\n    makes the learning curve's labeled counts and the method's\n   \
      \ actual scoring state disagree.\n\nReference skeleton \u2014 keep this structure;\
      \ adapt names to the spec:\n\n    import numpy as np\n    labeled_idx = np.asarray(initial_indices)\n\
      \    unlabeled_idx = np.setdiff1d(np.arange(len(x_pool)), labeled_idx)\n   \
      \ learning_curve = []\n\n    def train_eval_current(round_seed):\n        model\
      \ = build_model(...)                    # FRESH \u2192 retrain from scratch\n\
      \        model = train_from_scratch(\n            model, x_pool[labeled_idx],\
      \ y_pool[labeled_idx],\n            ..., seed=round_seed)\n        acc = evaluate(model,\
      \ x_test, y_test)\n        learning_curve.append((len(labeled_idx), acc))\n\
      \        return model\n\n    model = train_eval_current(SEED)              \
      \   # initial labeled set\n    for r in range(cfg[\"num_rounds\"]):\n      \
      \  pos = select_batch(\n            model, x_pool[unlabeled_idx], cfg[\"batch_size\"\
      ], SEED + r)\n        chosen = unlabeled_idx[np.asarray(pos)]      # positions\
      \ \u2192 GLOBAL indices\n        labeled_idx = np.union1d(labeled_idx, chosen)\n\
      \        unlabeled_idx = np.setdiff1d(unlabeled_idx, chosen)\n        model\
      \ = train_eval_current(SEED + r + 1)     # post-acquisition eval\n\n\xA75.1\
      \ trains and evaluates the initial labeled set, then trains and\nevaluates after\
      \ each acquisition round. The curve must reflect the\nretrained model, not the\
      \ warmup. Print per-round status.\n"
  - id: learning_curve
    title: '### 5.2 Learning curve'
    content: 'Plot learning_curve as a single line chart (labels acquired vs.

      test accuracy). Title names the method + dataset + smoke-sized.

      '
- id: own_data
  title: '## 6. Use your own data'
  kind: agnostic
  content: 'Two options (Option A: pass an explicit path; Option B: drop file in

    method/example_data/ to override default), three formats (.pt / .json

    / .csv) with examples of each, architecture-swap note pointing at

    method/model.py for image-shaped tensors.

    '
```
